{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.5,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R98"],
      "pins": ["R98.1", "R98.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R98 is valued '24k' in the netlist and SPICE deck, but its library description and MPN describe a 24Ω part (FRC0805J240TSD, LCSC C2930261). The value and the purchased part disagree by three orders of magnitude.",
      "expected": "The schematic value of R98 should match the 24Ω part actually specified, or the BOM part should be changed to a 24kΩ resistor.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R98\") (value \"24k\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R98 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the 24Ω part is fitted, it places a heavy load across the high-voltage rail VOUTN–VOUTP, which will load or disrupt the high-voltage generator and dissipate significant power. If the schematic value is intended, the BOM is wrong and the wrong part will be assembled.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D7", "D11", "D35", "R38", "R15", "R11"],
      "pins": ["D7.2", "D11.2", "D35.2"],
      "nets": ["/NET0099"],
      "observed": "The anodes of D7, D11 and D35 (the status LEDs) are joined only to each other on net /NET0099. No supply rail, resistor or driver is connected to that net, so the LED anode is floating. Their cathodes go to the Ethernet/Pi status signals through R38, R15 and R11.",
      "expected": "The common anode of these indicator LEDs should be tied to +3V3, as the other status LEDs in the design are (for example D33 and D4 have their anodes on +3V3).",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"22\") (name \"/NET0099\") (class \"Default\")\n      (node (ref \"D11\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))\n      (node (ref \"D35\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))\n      (node (ref \"D7\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D33\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The Ethernet and Pi activity indicator LEDs cannot light, so these status indications are lost. This is a functional omission, not a safety-critical failure.",
      "confidence": 0.35
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["D16", "R73"],
      "pins": ["D16.2", "D16.4", "R73.1", "R73.2"],
      "nets": ["Net-(D16-K2)", "/NET0177", "NET0177"],
      "observed": "R73 connects the cathode pin K2 of dual LED D16 (net Net-(D16-K2)) to net NET0177, which is the same net as the anode A2 (D16 pin 4) and the U53 output. The series resistor therefore shorts the LED's own anode and cathode, bypassing the LED channel.",
      "expected": "The K2 cathode should be current-limited through R73 to ground (as K1 is through R3), not returned to the same node as the anode.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R73\") (value \"130R\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D16\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R73\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R3\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The second LED channel of D16 never lights correctly, and the drive path is wrong for the e-stop status indication. The fault is at schematic level and would persist in every build.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The clearest deviation is the R98 value of 24k, which contradicts its 24Ω library description and MPN. Two lower-confidence wiring issues were also found: the floating anode net of D7/D11/D35 and a cathode-to-anode resistor loop on D16. The rest of the power, CAN, SPI and USB wiring appears consistent with the spec."
}

anomalies.observed: R98 is valued '24k' in the netlist and SPICE deck, but its library description and MPN describe a 24Ω part (FRC0805J240TSD, LCSC C2930261). The value and the purchased part disagree by three orders of magnitude.
anomalies.expected: The schematic value of R98 should match the 24Ω part actually specified, or the BOM part should be changed to a 24kΩ resistor.

evidence.quote: (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the 24Ω part is fitted, it places a heavy load across the high-voltage rail VOUTN–VOUTP, which will load or disrupt the high-voltage generator and dissipate significant power. If the schematic value is intended, the BOM is wrong and the wrong part will be assembled.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of D7, D11 and D35 (the status LEDs) are joined only to each other on net /NET0099. No supply rail, resistor or driver is connected to that net, so the LED anode is floating. Their cathodes go to the Ethernet/Pi status signals through R38, R15 and R11.
anomalies.expected: The common anode of these indicator LEDs should be tied to +3V3, as the other status LEDs in the design are (for example D33 and D4 have their anodes on +3V3).
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet and Pi activity indicator LEDs cannot light, so these status indications are lost. This is a functional omission, not a safety-critical failure.

anomalies.observed: R73 connects the cathode pin K2 of dual LED D16 (net Net-(D16-K2)) to net NET0177, which is the same net as the anode A2 (D16 pin 4) and the U53 output. The series resistor therefore shorts the LED's own anode and cathode, bypassing the LED channel.
anomalies.expected: The K2 cathode should be current-limited through R73 to ground (as K1 is through R3), not returned to the same node as the anode.
anomalies.impact: The second LED channel of D16 never lights correctly, and the drive path is wrong for the e-stop status indication. The fault is at schematic level and would persist in every build.
